confidence_notes: I ran 5 web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Rome prices. The food and drink anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living sources, mainly Numbeo figures republished by Expatica (June 2026), plus Housing Anywhere, Expatistan and a few guides. Those sources were reported in EUR and I converted at about 1.17 USD per EUR, an approximation I did not source from the RBA. Source figures: inexpensive meal about EUR 15.6; cappuccino about EUR 2.1 (higher when seated); 0.5 l draught beer about EUR 5.2 (Expatistan pub beer EUR 5.9); three-course meal for two about EUR 62-65; cocktail about EUR 11-12. I found no aggregated price for a glass of wine, so I estimated it at about EUR 6 from the beer price and anecdotal guides, which range from EUR 3-6 at budget wine bars to EUR 8-12 at tourist venues. The RBA figure came from search-result text describing the RBA exchange-rate page. I did not open the page myself. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates for a July high-season window. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages, so they carry the most uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was used. Food and drink anchors are based directly on Rome price aggregates. Hostel and hotel anchors reflect general knowledge of Rome as a high-demand Southern European tourist capital in peak season, roughly in line with other major Italian and Western European destinations.
